races.name: Champagne Pommery Brut Rose Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Consistent performer at 10f on Good ground with six recent second-place finishes in similar conditions, making this trip and going combination a clear comfort zone; natural hold-up horse whose strong sim-going record (8 runs, 2 wins, 6 placed) makes him the standout closer in this field under Kieran Shoemark.
runners_data.comment: Falcon Nine has been runner-up three times in his last six starts, most recently 11 days ago, and arrives fit and well-handicapped on our rating; he has experience over today's trip and conditions, and from stall seven carries 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Samra Star
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on Good ground and boasts a recent placed effort at 9f, suggesting the step up to 1m1f is at least workable; in truth she races from the rear, so she'll need Gemini Man to set enough pace — Paul Mulrennan has to ride patiently regardless of where the map places her.
runners_data.comment: Samra Star arrives here on the back of a win last time out and a second before that, boasting experience over today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that eighth earlier in her recent form hints at some inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Miners Gamble
runners_data.note: Struggling for form with a run of 5-9-8-6-9 finishes across Standard and Soft ground, and the switch to Good turf at Musselburgh is a minor positive; rides as a natural hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the overcrowded rear rather than any change in Luke Morris's likely tactics.
runners_data.comment: Miners Gamble has run over today's trip and going before and, returning on a sharp 13-day turnaround, is fit enough to go close; our rating of 57 ranks him fourth of the seven, though winless in his last six starts, that lack of a win is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has two wins and three placed efforts from nine runs on Good going, the best going-record in this field, and his last-time-out win over 8f on Good shows he retains ability; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is useful, though the step to 1m1f is a question given his best form has come at shorter.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out makes him hard to fancy despite a win one start back, and a struggling trainer strike-rate of 5% over the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence. He has run over today's trip and going, and 11 days between runs suggests he's fit.

runners_data.name: Liberty Looming
runners_data.note: Habitual stayer who has been running over 13f-17f in recent starts, so this drop to 1m1f represents a dramatic shortening of trip that is hard to see suiting; his sim-going record (12 runs, zero wins, zero placed) on turf Good is a significant red flag, and Adam Nicol's trainer record of 0/4 over 14 days offers no compensating confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Liberty Looming faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp seven-day turnaround in good enough order from stall two carrying 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ flag for fading in finishes, which is a notable concern in a race where a single front-runner may set a flat pace that suits horses who sustain their effort rather than quicken; Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's four-year-old does have two placed efforts on Good ground at 8f-10f under Lexie Clarkson (7lb claim), but the finishing tendency limits his ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Toy Soldier has shown real consistency at this level, finishing second in two of his last six starts, and he returns in good order just 18 days after his last outing — experience over today's trip and going is a further asset. The risk is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Gemini Man
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner and the sole pace-setter in a field of seven, giving him an uncontested lead at whatever tempo he chooses over a trip (10f) at which he has recent winning form; his STYLE_FIT tag as a Prominent type mapped forward accurately reflects his role here, and Iain Jardine's yard form means he arrives in decent condition.
runners_data.comment: Gemini Man ran second last time out in a pleasing return to form, though a pulled up effort two starts back is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and his two wins in his last six starts suggest he retains ability, but 130 lb is a stern test.

races.paceDynamic: Gemini Man is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m1f handicap and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge him, he should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. The remainder of the field — Falcon Nine, Samra Star, Miners Gamble, Approaching Dawn, Liberty Looming, and Toy Soldier — are all natural hold-up horses, meaning Gemini Man faces no meaningful early pressure and can control the fractions entirely on his own terms. This creates a classic front-runner's paradise: a single honest but uncontested lead, a steady pace through the middle portion of the race, and a final-furlong test that rewards those who have conserved energy behind a sensible gallop rather than burning through it chasing a breakaway. This field holds more hold-up types than a single race shape can naturally accommodate; of those redistributed to midfield on the map, Approaching Dawn (best recent form and course-relevant going stats) and Falcon Nine (consistent second-place finishes at this distance/going combo) are best placed to convert a prominent-chasing position into a winning one. The race shape firmly favours hold-up horses with a sharp late turn of foot or those who can track Gemini Man from just off the pace, provided the tempo stays honest enough to bring them into play — a front-runner dictating his own terms must be respected.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gemini Man Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man bowls along at a comfortable gallop and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Gemini Man sets a controlled pace with no rival willing or able to press him, conserving enough in the tank to repel challengers in the final furlong on Good ground at Musselburgh; his Iain Jardine yard is in strong form (5/27 over 14 days) and his OR-53 represents a competitive weight at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough to stretch the field and a hold-up runner with a sharp turn of foot arrives in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A steady but not crawling gallop set by Gemini Man leaves enough tempo for genuine closers to pick off a tiring leader; Falcon Nine, who has finished second on six occasions on Good ground at 10f, or Approaching Dawn, with two wins from nine on comparable going, are best positioned to benefit from a strong late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Looms
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man sets a falsely slow gallop and the midfield pack bunches, turning the finish into a sprint.
scenarios.body: A crawl of a pace compresses the field into a tight group rounding the final bend, gifting horses with a sharp sprint finish an advantage regardless of their natural style; Toy Soldier (two placed efforts on Good in 2024) and Samra Star (winner on Good, last time out) carry enough pace to benefit if the race degenerates into a dash.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Wide Draw Winner
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys mis-read the pace and multiple hold-up horses attempt to force position simultaneously, creating a messy, compressed race.
scenarios.body: Several horses mapped out of their natural role attempt to settle closer than usual, creating traffic problems through the middle of the race and a chaotic finish that rewards any horse finding a clear passage; Liberty Looming, step back sharply in trip from habitual 13f-17f distances, is unlikely to benefit, but Miners Gamble could steal into contention if the pace scrambles.

watchPoints.text: Watch Gemini Man's early fractions — if Jack Nicholls (3) sends him clear at a very slow gallop, the hold-up horses mapped to midfield will have almost no pace to chase down and the race devolves into a sprint, fundamentally changing which horses benefit.

Approaching Dawn's jockey Lauren Young (5lb claimer) will face a tactical challenge: the horse's natural hold-up style in a field bunched at the rear means she must judge when to commit, and mistiming it risks being trapped wide or flat-footed at Musselburgh's sharp final turn.

Liberty Looming is stepping down from 13f-17f trips to 1m1f — watch the early stages for signs of keenness or discomfort at the shorter distance, which could unsettle the rear of the field if she fails to settle.

Toy Soldier's flagged tendency to fade in the finish becomes more significant if Gemini Man sets a genuinely honest pace — any horse who races prominently and ties up in the final furlong could cause interference for closers arriving late from behind.

Iain Jardine saddles two runners — Gemini Man and Falcon Nine — which creates an implicit stable dynamic: Gemini Man's front-running role may effectively serve as a pacemaker that sets up the race for his stablemate Falcon Nine arriving from the rear.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Barnaby Rudge
runners_data.note: Two wins from two starts, both over 5f on soft and standard ground, gives James Fanshawe's juvenile a strong form platform; a natural front-runner who will battle My Mate Fitz for the lead, and the question is whether that energy expenditure compromises his finishing effort in the final 100 yards.

runners_data.name: Minster Man
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's hold-up juvenile placed on good ground last time and brings the most relevant going profile in the field with a 1/1 record on similar conditions; Paul Mulrennan will be content to let the pace duel unfold ahead and pounce, though Musselburgh's sharp 5f may not offer quite enough time for a rear-held finisher to fully wind up.

runners_data.name: My Mate Fitz
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner has finished sixth and fourth in both outings and arrives with modest form figures, yet is confirmed as a front-runner who will press Barnaby Rudge hard from the off; that willingness to race prominently is more of a liability than an asset here given the rival pace presence, making it difficult to fancy him to sustain the effort over the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Sod Hall Lane
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's entry carries a complete information blackout — no last-run date, no form string, and a running style logged as unknown — making any assessment speculative; lightly raced status on good ground over 5f means the market move, if any, will be the only real indicator of intent.

runners_data.name: Faith In Florence
runners_data.note: Ed Walker has had an excellent 14-day strike rate (11/40) and Kieran Shoemark rides a horse that placed twice in two starts, both over 6f on good ground; dropping to 5f is a query given both runs came at longer, but prominent tactics could allow her to slot just off the pace duel and grab a share if the front pair tire.

races.paceDynamic: Barnaby Rudge and My Mate Fitz are both confirmed front-runners, meaning this 5f at Musselburgh will ignite immediately from the gates with two horses competing hard for the early lead on good ground. That direct, unrelenting duel is likely to set an honest-to-brisk gallop across the first two furlongs, burning energy from both principals and ensuring the race is genuinely run rather than dawdling. Faith In Florence, the one prominent type in the field, will attempt to track the speed and could benefit if the front pair weaken each other, while Minster Man from the back and the unknown Sod Hall Lane will be relying on a fast-run race to bring them into it late. This race shape most clearly favours a prominent or late-finishing profile — any horse able to sit just off the contested pace without expending early energy stands to inherit if the two leaders overcook it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dual Pace Duel, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Barnaby Rudge and My Mate Fitz fight hard for the lead and drain each other through the first half of the race.
scenarios.body: The contested gallop leaves both leaders vulnerable in the final furlong, opening the door for anything tracking behind them; Faith In Florence pressing from a prominent position or Minster Man finishing with purpose from the rear are the logical inheritors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners asserts cleanly and the other drops away, allowing a controlled lead to be held.
scenarios.body: Barnaby Rudge, unbeaten in two and trained by James Fanshawe, has the stronger recent form record and could prove the stronger of the pair, dictating terms at a manageable pace that preserves his finishing kick; on good ground with a clean breakaway, a wire-to-wire outcome becomes plausible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Sod Hall Lane, lightly raced and a complete unknown, possesses a level of raw ability that renders the pace dynamic academic.
scenarios.body: Declan Carroll's runner has no public form to assess and the absence of a last-run date heightens the uncertainty, but debut or near-debut types on good ground at 5f can capitalise on a strongly-run race if they carry natural speed; the honest gallop set by the leaders gives any genuinely talented newcomer a true test to shine.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Front Pair Survive
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel between Barnaby Rudge and My Mate Fitz proves less intense than expected and they settle into a moderate rhythm.
scenarios.body: A softer early pace would neutralise the hold-up advantage for Minster Man and allow the front pair to coast into the straight relatively fresh, with Barnaby Rudge's unbeaten juvenile profile making him the more likely beneficiary; Faith In Florence's prominent style also suits if the race is not truly run.

watchPoints.text: Watch the early battle between Barnaby Rudge and My Mate Fitz — whichever establishes the lead cleanest will have a significant energy advantage heading into the final two furlongs, and a prolonged head-to-head duel between them could compromise both.

Minster Man's finishing effort hinges on the pace being genuinely strong; if the tempo drops even slightly, Paul Mulrennan's hold-up position becomes increasingly difficult to recover from on a tight 5f course like Musselburgh.

Sod Hall Lane is a total unknown — monitor market moves in the minutes before post time, as any significant support from the Declan Carroll yard for a lightly-raced runner with no public form is meaningful information.

Faith In Florence has run exclusively over 6f in both career starts; the drop to 5f is untested and how quickly she breaks and settles into a tracking position behind the pace will determine whether she has enough runway to be involved at the finish.

races.name: Copper Blossom Ladies Day Nursery Selling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Extended Order
runners_data.note: Has won and placed at exactly 7f on Good turf (sim-going 2/3), giving solid course-and-distance credentials under Daniel Muscutt; a hold-up type who will need the pace to collapse or travel close enough to pounce — the ⚠ fading flag is a real concern if this becomes a test of finishing stamina rather than a sprint burst.|
runners_data.comment: Extended Order landed a win three starts back and returns on a sharp 21-day turnaround with distance experience in his favour, drawing stall 3 carrying 135 lb; the risk is that he has been unplaced in his last two starts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's juvenile has a strong recent form string (866123) and a genuine win at 7f on Good ground in latest, showing progressive form at this trip; by nature a hold-up horse, though the pace map has it positioned in midfield given the density of rear-runners in this field, meaning it may be forced to race closer to the pace than it would ideally prefer.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked last of five on our figures, Amantha faces a stiff ask, though her recent form has improved markedly — a winner three starts back, second two starts back, and third last time out — and she has run over today's distance and going before, returning on a sharp seven-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Bella Lucia
runners_data.note: Style is unclassified (U), making her a genuine tactical wildcard — William Pyle takes the ride for Gemma Tutty whose stable is 2/16 over 14 days; all three runs have been at shorter distances (5–6f) so this is a significant step up in trip, and her sole Good-going run produced a sixth, making her impact on the race shape and outcome hard to project.|
runners_data.comment: Bella Lucia has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third two of her last three starts, and has run over today's trip before — she comes here just 15 days fresh and looks a solid danger. The main risk is she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides a filly with five career outings all on Good ground, placing twice from five at 7f — her best form aligns closely with today's conditions; a hold-up operator who will need the field to come back to her in the straight, and her recent record (form 69722) shows consistency at the rear of the field rather than winning form.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts, Bigalo has posted back-to-back runner-up finishes and has experience over today's trip and conditions — he's winless in his last five but the placed form is solid, and our rating has him narrowly on top here.

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's two-year-old wears a hood and is the race's only confirmed front-runner, with a win at 7f on Good going in her latest outing; she is mapped as prominent (P) with a STYLE_FIT of 0.93, suggesting she may not entirely command the pace as freely as her label implies, but with no rival likely to chase her hard she still holds the clearest positional advantage.|
runners_data.comment: Bluestone Lady arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a live threat at 129 lb from stall 4; the main risk is that unplaced run two starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Bluestone Lady is the lone confirmed front-runner in this five-strong field and, with no genuine rival prepared to chase her hard from the gate, she should be allowed to dictate a sustainable, unchallenged gallop over Musselburgh's flat seven furlongs. The hold-up contingent — Extended Order, Amantha, and Bigalo — will be tracking from behind, but with only one pace-setter setting an honest rather than a scorching tempo, the field is unlikely to be strung out early and the race will likely be run at a measured clip that keeps the bunch relatively compact into the home straight. Bella Lucia's style is uncertain (U), adding a small wildcard element to how the early order resolves, but she is unlikely to dramatically alter the tempo picture. With Bluestone Lady dictating a controlled pace and the closers needing a genuine furlong-and-a-half kick to reel her in, this shape favours prominent or just-off-the-pace runners who can travel within striking range and produce a finishing effort — pure hold-up horses dependent on a fast collapse of the pace are at a disadvantage. Note that the field carries more hold-up types than can realistically be accommodated at the rear, and Amantha has been redistributed to midfield on the map as it cannot secure its natural deep position with several rivals sharing that profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bluestone Lady Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bluestone Lady bowls along uncontested from the front and the hold-up horses fail to produce sufficient closing speed over Good turf.
scenarios.body: Bluestone Lady sets a measured, unchallenged fractions and simply refuses to be caught, her rivals struggling to mount a sustained run after tracking a pace that was never truly punishing; any prominent or just-off-the-pace horse that travels in her slipstream gets first crack at the prize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Bluestone Lady goes too fast early or the pace is stronger than expected, allowing closers to come with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-typical tempo would see the field spread out sooner, giving genuine hold-up types the energy differential they need to produce a finish; Bigalo's consistent placed form at 7f on Good ground makes it the best-placed closer to exploit this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Bella Lucia Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Lucia's unknown tactical style resolves into a prominent or pace-pressing role, injecting competition for the early lead.
scenarios.body: A contested pace puts pressure on Bluestone Lady's stamina reserves at this trip and opens the door for a runner with finishing speed; Bella Lucia stepping up sharply in trip from 5–6f adds uncertainty but also freshness to her challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Pace Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace results in a slow-run, bunched sprint home where tactical position and late luck dominate.
scenarios.body: With the field compressed through a slow opening, the result becomes a lottery in the final furlong and any runner who gets a clean run through can feature; Extended Order's top-speed profile and Bigalo's placed consistency give both a slim chance in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Bluestone Lady's hood and STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 mean she may not lead as dominantly as her front-runner label suggests — watch for any sign of reluctance or sluggish break from the gate that would fundamentally change the race shape.

Amantha is a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map — if it settles closer to the pace than usual under Luke Morris it could either improve its chance dramatically or burn out early, making it a key horse to track through the first two furlongs.

Extended Order carries a ⚠ fade flag from its form and is a hold-up type in a race likely to produce a steady pace — if it cannot land a prominent enough position to produce its effort at the right time, the fade tendency becomes a real risk late.

Bella Lucia's unknown style (U) at a trip she has never attempted (7f) means she could press Bluestone Lady for the lead unexpectedly — if she does, the pace dynamic shifts from controlled to contested and alters the outcome probability for every runner.

With five runners and a single front-runner, the pace is almost certain to be honest rather than fast — any observer should monitor early splits to confirm whether this becomes the steadily-run affair the map predicts or an uncharacteristically quick tempo that reshuffles the finishing order.

races.name: Champagne Pommery Cuvee Louise Gold Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jonny Concrete
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been consistent without winning recently (form -32441), goes well on Good ground with 3W7P in similar conditions, and Jack Nicholls' 3lb claim is a useful weight relief; needs to be on the premises rounding the home turn.
runners_data.comment: Jonny Concrete arrives on the back of a win last time out, is fit on a 14-day turnaround, and has experience over today's trip and conditions — our rating of 90 marks him as a strong threat. The main risk is whether he can defy a testing burden of 138 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Gweedore
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse whose recent form reads -70400 and whose sim-going record of 0W1P in comparable conditions is deeply uninspiring; Tom Eaves partners him but this looks a tough assignment off a 32-day break.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Gweedore nonetheless rates 96 on our figures — top of these eleven — and returns after 32 days having run over today's distance and going before; stall three and 137 lb to carry are the questions here.

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for David O'Meara and Daniel Tudhope who has finished between fifth and seventh in every one of his last five starts on Good ground (7/14 sim-going record, 0W0P); consistency in mediocrity makes it hard to find a winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Misunderstood has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 14-day turnaround in good order, with our rating of 90 marking him out as a live threat in this field — the risk is that he's winless in his last five starts, suggesting the breakthrough remains elusive.

runners_data.name: One Night Thunder
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by style — fitted with blinkers — who arrives off 13 days' rest with one win and three places in sim-going, but the crowded nature of the hold-up end of this field means he is unlikely to find his preferred position and must be marked down accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, One Night Thunder does at least bring distance-and-going experience to the table and returns on a sharp 13-day turnaround; however, a third three starts back is his only bright note in a largely moderate recent sequence, and 132 lb from stall 10 adds little comfort.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Three wins at 7f on Good ground and a recent course win make the form look strong on paper, but Jim Goldie's runner is a true hold-up type squeezed into a midfield role by race shape; Paul Mulrennan's experience may help, yet the tactical compromise is real.
runners_data.comment: Native Honey has won twice in his last six starts, but only a fifth last time out makes him hard to fancy, and a trainer firing at just 5% recently compounds the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, which counts for something.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's three-year-old has an outstanding sim-going record of 8/8 on comparable ground with one win and three places, and holds a prominent-to-midfield position that suits this shape better than deeper closers; the 28-day break is the main query.
runners_data.comment: Zarvali showed useful form when third two starts back and a winner four starts back, but a seventh last time out is harder to ignore; he has distance and going experience to call upon, though 129 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's second runner is another genuine hold-up type by running style — the 5lb claim of Lauren Young is attractive, but like stablemate Native Honey, Ashen is a natural closer who will struggle to operate freely with several hold-up types competing for the same ground at the back.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Ashen is hard to fancy for all that he has experience of today's trip and going, draws stall one, and returns on a quick turnaround with a win in his last six starts to his name.

runners_data.name: Eagle Bay
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner for Harriet Bethell and Sean Bowen, unbeaten in two completed starts with a win on soft and a win on Good giving him a 1W2P sim-going record; 41 days off the track is the only note of caution on an otherwise clear pace-map profile.
runners_data.comment: Eagle Bay arrives on the back of two wins in his last three starts, with experience of today's distance and going in his favour, but carrying 136 lb from stall 11, our rating puts him well below the field's leading lights, making him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Passing Thought
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has the most powerful recent form in the prominent group — two wins from six starts including a 7f Good win — and Kieran Shoemark has ridden him before; the trainer's 11/40 14-day strike rate is the strongest in the field and this runner fits the scenario-B profile most cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Passing Thought has won twice in her last five starts, including a victory two starts back, and has run over today's distance and going — a trainer firing at 26% over the past fortnight adds strong confidence; the concern is whether 49 days off has left her short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Vixey
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has had nine starts on comparable going but only found three wins and seven places across a longer career; recent form of 35-820 is flat and the OR 79 puts her in a competitive middle bracket, while the step back to 7f from recent 8f runs is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a second two runs back shows she retains ability; Vixey has run over today's trip and going, and 10 days since her latest outing leaves her fresh, but her most recent run was unplaced and she ranks eighth of eleven on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Augustus Gloop
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old drops back from 7-8f to 7f on Good, which matches four of his five recent runs, but his form of 1-2674 shows a horse who has not recaptured his best; Daniel Muscutt takes over and the prominent style puts him in the right tactical lane at least.
runners_data.comment: Augustus Gloop showed a win and a second in recent starts but has since dropped to finishes of sixth and seventh, and was only fourth last time out; he has run over today's trip and steps back in from stall five carrying 133 lb, though that dip in form gives pause.

races.paceDynamic: Eagle Bay is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to press from the front, should dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 7f trip on Good ground at Musselburgh. Passing Thought, Jonny Concrete, Augustus Gloop, and Vixey will push for prominent positions just behind, creating a bunched chasing pack but not the kind of fierce early pressure that destabilises a front-runner. The field carries a significant hold-up contingent — One Night Thunder, Native Honey, and Ashen are genuine closers by nature but are redistributed into a midfield mapping because there simply is not enough rear-running space in this shape for all three to operate naturally, reducing their effectiveness. With the pace controlled and honest rather than brutal, this race shape strongly favours the confirmed front-runner Eagle Bay and the prominent racers able to travel just behind the leader, as a moderate early tempo will leave little to close on from further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eagle Bay Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Eagle Bay bowls along in front at a comfortable tempo with no rival willing or able to press him.
scenarios.body: Eagle Bay sets a sustainable fractions-based gallop, the prominent chasers burn energy trying to close but find the leader has conserved enough to kick clear in the final furlong; Musselburgh's flat 7f suits a front-runner who controls the race from the gun.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chasers Peg Him Back
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched prominent group — Passing Thought, Jonny Concrete, or Augustus Gloop — apply enough pressure to deny Eagle Bay a clean lead.
scenarios.body: Eagle Bay is forced to use more energy than ideal maintaining his position, and one of the prominent cover horses exploits the slightly stronger tempo to arrive fresh in the straight; Passing Thought's recent course-distance win and Ed Walker's strong 11/40 14-day form makes him the likeliest beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Picks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Eagle Bay fades badly in the final two furlongs, leaving a gap for a midfield tracker to thread through.
scenarios.body: A horse tucked just off the pace with tactical awareness — Zarvali, who has excellent sim-going figures of 8/8 on this ground, or Native Honey with three wins at 7f on Good — could thread a path late; however, with Native Honey carrying the REDISTRIBUTED caveat as a true hold-up type unlikely to get its preferred position, Zarvali is better placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring the redistributed hold-up horses into play from their actual deep positions.
scenarios.body: One Night Thunder, Native Honey, and Ashen are all natural hold-up types but are fighting against a race shape that will not play to their strengths today; only a truly strong gallop and a well-timed run by a jockey of the calibre of Paul Mulrennan on Native Honey gives this scenario any credibility.

watchPoints.text: Eagle Bay (front-runner) — watch whether Sean Bowen sets a genuinely controlled gallop or is nudged into a stronger pace by the prominent group; his entire chance hinges on controlling tempo from the front.

Passing Thought and Jonny Concrete — these two are the most likely prominent horses to press Eagle Bay if they break sharply; if either hunts the leader aggressively before halfway, the race switches from Scenario A to Scenario B.

Native Honey and One Night Thunder — both are genuine hold-up types who will be searching for a gap that may not exist in a compact field; watch for signs they are unable to find daylight until too late.

Zarvali — her sim-going record of 8/8 on comparable ground is the best strike-rate percentage in the field; if Eagle Bay weakens late, she is the most likely midfield beneficiary given her tactical position and ground affinity.

Augustus Gloop and Vixey — both prominent types in a cluster chasing Eagle Bay; if they over-race or are covered up too early, neither has the late acceleration to come from off the pace, making their positioning in the first two furlongs critical.

races.name: Champagne Pommery Brut Royal Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: David & Nicola Barron handler is 0-from-8 in the last 14 days and this 6-year-old's 0-from-4 record on similar going underlines a habit of placing without winning; a true hold-up horse who needs a stronger pace than Big Fun is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Jer Batt has finished third three times in his last five starts and returns on a quick turnaround just seven days after his latest effort, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; winless in recent starts, but our rating of 93 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is the standout jockey booking here and Tiva's 13-from-15 Good-ground strikes including two wins show a clear affinity for today's conditions; a natural hold-up performer who will need to be sharper from the gate than usual given the expected lack of pressure up front.
runners_data.comment: Tiva ran third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her key experience; winless in her last six starts, though, and that lack of a win remains the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's yard is ticking along at 2-from-40 in the last fortnight and this 4-year-old has shown genuine prominence, making it the only realistic challenger to Big Fun for an early position; a two-place record from nine Good-ground runs suggests it finds a way to place but the 136lb burden is notable.
runners_data.comment: Montezuma has been knocking on the door in recent starts — second last time out and third two starts back — and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the worry is his trainer is in a lean spell at just 5% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Big Fun
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 3-year-old is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and shapes to lead uncontested on Good ground over 5f; the 68-day absence is the only credible threat to its chance, and the STYLE_FIT flag serves as a mild caution rather than a serious concern given it maps naturally to the lead position.
runners_data.comment: Big Fun won four starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating puts him well clear of his official mark — strong credentials for a bold show from stall one. The main risk is a return from 68 days off.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type — in reality sitting much further back than this map's midfield placement suggests — whose six consecutive placings, including five in a row finishing second, underline its tenacity without winning; the 5-pound claimer Lauren Young softens the weight but the lack of a truly run race is the primary obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts despite a string of runner-up finishes, Woohoo faces a stiff ask ranked fifth of six on our figures, and a trainer striking at just 5% in the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence; she has run over today's trip and going, at least.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: John Ryan's 3-year-old is the lowest-rated runner (OR 65) and, despite solid Going exposure (12-from-14 on similar ground), a form string reading 549865 offers little encouragement; structurally a hold-up horse pushed forward on the map due to field congestion at the rear, which compounds the challenge of making ground in a potentially slowly-run 5f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a best recent finish of fourth, Ecclefechan makes little appeal ranked last of six on our figures despite having run over today's trip and going before; 120 lb from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Big Fun is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should coast to the front from stall and dictate at a sustainable, measured gallop over this flat 5f on Good ground. Jer Batt, Tiva, Woohoo, and Ecclefechan are all hold-up horses by nature, meaning the pace map is dense at the rear — the field holds more true hold-up types than the map can place, and Montezuma is the only realistic challenger to Big Fun for a prominent position, leaving Big Fun effectively uncontested in front. This unchallenged leader sets a controlled pace that heavily favours horses racing prominently or from just off the lead, as the sectionals are unlikely to be severe enough to cause a leader to stop — closers will need to be sharp from the gate to have any hope of reeling in a horse who has had it all its own way. The race shape squarely rewards a prominent, well-positioned runner who can travel into the steady pace and pounce; pure hold-up horses are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Big Fun Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Big Fun jumps cleanly and Montezuma settles into second without applying early pressure, leaving the leader to dictate a controlled tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Big Fun sets fractions entirely to suit itself, taking the sting out of the race for hold-up horses who never get close enough to strike; the compact 5f with a flat profile means a comfortable leader rarely gets caught if the pace is honest but not frantic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Montezuma pushes up to challenge Big Fun from the outset and the two fight for supremacy, lifting the pace enough to set up a finish.
scenarios.body: The elevated early tempo burns off Big Fun and leaves Montezuma vulnerable late, opening a window for the sharpest hold-up horse to arrive with a late burst; Tiva's excellent 13-from-15 Good-ground record and Daniel Tudhope's positional intelligence make it the most credible beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and Big Fun fades in the final furlong, allowing a closer to pick off tired rivals.
scenarios.body: Jer Batt or Tiva, both genuine hold-up horses with solid Good-ground form at 5f, would need to switch off cleanly and produce a strong late surge, but their redistribution to midfield on this map reflects the structural reality that they are unlikely to get close enough in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Big Fun's 68-day layoff shows in a sluggish start or a mid-race flat spot, scrambling the expected race order.
scenarios.body: Woohoo's relentless placed record (eight placings from thirteen starts on Good ground) suggests it fights on gamely when the pace is competitive, and Ecclefechan at a low OR could creep into contention unnoticed — though both are true hold-up types squeezed forward on the map and face real positional hurdles.

watchPoints.text: Big Fun's 68-day layoff is the pivotal factor — watch the pre-race paddock closely for any sign of condition loss, as an unfit leader who ties up late hands the race to Montezuma or Tiva.

Montezuma's early positioning will shape the entire race — if Paul Mulrennan sends it forward to press Big Fun, the pace lifts and hold-up horses suddenly become live; watch the first two furlongs carefully.

Woohoo has finished second five times in recent starts and its jockey Lauren Young (5lb claim) may be tempted to ride more prominently than the horse's natural style warrants — a change in tactics could scramble the expected race shape.

Tiva's headgear notation (tv = tongue tie and visor) is worth monitoring; Daniel Tudhope regularly produces strong finishes on Good ground at 5f for O'Meara and the combination has strong course-going credentials entering today.

Ecclefechan is 21 days off a run and races for a trainer who is 0-from-4 in the last fortnight — flag as a potential drifter in the market rather than a market mover, which would shift scenario probabilities if money arrives late.

races.name: Brodie Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roc De Fer
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo for Sir Mark Prescott who has won back-to-back over 11-12f on Tapeta; steps up in trip on turf Good for the first time but trainer has strong 7/26 14-day record and Luke Morris partnership is live — prominent style suits an uncontested-pace scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Roc De Fer arrives in cracking nick, winning his last two starts and with his trainer firing at 31% over the past fortnight. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 80 marks him out as the one to beat, though the 141 lb burden is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Consistent 8yo with solid form in this grade on Good ground (2W, 5P from 13 comparable starts) and a genuine hold-up specialist; races in a tongue-tie and has been placing regularly over 13-16f, representing Gary Rutherford who has been quiet lately — his natural trailing style is authentic and well-suited to finishing off a controlled tempo.
runners_data.comment: Simple Star shaped with promise when second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going bolsters his claims under 139 lb; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and must find more on recent form.

runners_data.name: Sure And Stedfast
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Ewan Whillans whose last two starts have produced places over 11-13f on Good; returns after 27 days and has struggled on Tapeta, so the turf switch is in his favour — jockey Greg Fairley needs to find clear daylight late on a tight Musselburgh circuit.
runners_data.comment: Consistently hitting the frame — third last time out and a second three starts back — Sure And Stedfast arrives on a good freshness angle at 27 days, has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 74 suggests he's ahead of his official mark; the risk is he's yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Tommy's Promise
runners_data.note: Front-running/prominent type who won twice over 10f on Tapeta but has shown little over 12f on a similar surface; now trying 1m5f turf for the first time after a 126-day break, and Tom Eaves takes over — the absence and step up in trip are both unproven quantities that temper his claims.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 126 days makes Tommy's Promise hard to trust here, and ranked last on our figures he faces a stiff task; ninth last time out compounds the concern. He has run over today's trip and going, and two wins in his last five starts show there is ability to unearth if fit.

runners_data.name: Alnayef
runners_data.note: Won over 13f Good last time out for Jim Goldie, confirming he handles this trip and going well; Paul Mulrennan is a strong booking and Goldie has two winners from 40 recent runners — a true hold-up horse whose authentic closing style is genuinely suited to arriving late off a lone front-runner's controlled gallop.
runners_data.comment: Alnayef showed up well with a third last time out and was a winner two starts back, but the trainer's current 5% strike rate over the last 14 days is a concern, and he carries a hefty 136 lb here.

runners_data.name: Willow Wood
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo is the confirmed pace-setter and will enjoy an uncontested lead on Good ground over this trip; her two wins came on Soft and Tapeta respectively and she has not won or placed on turf Good (0W, 0P in 2 starts), which is a surface concern even if her tactical role gives her the clearest advantage in the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked sixth of seven on our figures and carrying 132 lb, Willow Wood faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive on the back of a win two starts back and has previous experience on today's going; the trainer's 26% strike rate over the past fortnight offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Much
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 3yo is fitted with a tongue-tie and races from a hold-up position; has run well over 12f on Tapeta but form on Good turf is limited to two below-par efforts, and stepping back up in trip after a 7-day turnaround means stamina under this race shape is the key unknown for Daniel Muscutt.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and carrying 130 lb, Much has run over today's trip and going before, and his rating of 72 edges his official mark — making him a lively danger. The main risk is he's winless in his last four starts.

races.paceDynamic: Willow Wood is the confirmed lone front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her early, she will set a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m5f trip on Good ground at Musselburgh. Roc De Fer and Tommy's Promise are the only other prominent-style runners and will likely sit just off the leader, creating an orderly two-tier formation rather than a contested pace scenario. This race shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter dictating a measured tempo — strongly favours hold-up horses with finishing kick, provided they can close the gap in the final two furlongs; the field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and Simple Star and Alnayef are genuine closers who are most likely to secure their preferred back-of-field berth, with Much also expected to race from deep. The tactical verdict is clear: a patient closer who can produce a sustained run over the rising ground late will be best served by this uncontested-lead shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Willow Wood Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Willow Wood leads throughout at a controlled tempo and the field never seriously challenges her early lead.
scenarios.body: Willow Wood sets a moderate, metronomic gallop and the lack of genuine pace competition means she conserves energy, arriving at the final turn in front and kicking on; horses tracking her closely from the prominent positions, specifically Roc De Fer, benefit from the slipstream and the steady tempo that blunts the closers' finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Willow Wood is slow enough to compress the field and allow the genuine closers to arrive with a single powerful run in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Simple Star, who has solid form over this trip on Good ground and boasts 13 places from 15 outings in similar conditions, and Alnayef, a recent winner over 13f on Good, both launch from the rear; if the tempo has been honest enough to stop the leader sprinting clear, a closer can get up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Upstage Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Roc De Fer or Tommy's Promise press Willow Wood harder than expected, lifting the pace and setting up a battle among the forward group that drains the leader.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would compromise Willow Wood's stamina reserves and leave Roc De Fer, who has won at 12f on Tapeta and has been improving, or Tommy's Promise, a dual 10f course winner returning after 126 days fresh, to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is truly crawling and the race turns into a sprint finish from 2f out, suiting a horse with a sharp change of gear over middle distances.
scenarios.body: Much, stepping up from shorter on turf with headgear and trained by James Fanshawe, and Sure And Stedfast, who has placed twice over this sort of trip on Good, could benefit from a bunched finish that negates positional disadvantages; this scenario is least likely given the field size and Musselburgh's galloping track demanding genuine stamina.

watchPoints.text: Willow Wood's uncontested lead is the pivotal factor — if she secures the front without any pressure from Roc De Fer or Tommy's Promise, she is likely to control every aspect of the race shape and expose the closers to a long-range kick they cannot match.

Alnayef's recent 13f Good winner form is the most relevant piece of form in the race — watch whether Paul Mulrennan can extricate him from a potentially congested group of hold-up types in the straight with clear running room.

Tommy's Promise's 126-day absence combined with a first run over 1m5f on turf is a significant compound risk; if he is not fully wound up he could drop away and disrupt the rhythm of horses immediately behind him rather than contributing to the pace he is mapped to provide.

Simple Star, Sure And Stedfast, Alnayef, and Much all want to race from the rear, creating a cluster of closers who will need to fan wide or find gaps in the straight — track bias and draw at Musselburgh over this trip may determine which of them gets a clear, unimpeded run to the line.

Roc De Fer's Prescott/Morris combination with a strong trainer 14-day strike rate (7/26) and back-to-back wins is worth monitoring in running — if he tracks Willow Wood in second he is the horse most likely to pounce if she idles or flattens out.

races.name: Muirhall Energy Breath Of Fresh Energy Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Filey Beach
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two course wins at 7f on good ground and strong similar-going form (3W from 9 comparable runs); wears headgear, trained by Ruth Carr who is 5/27 over 14 days, and carries top weight of 135lbs — the key question is whether that burden blunts her in the closing stages of an uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Filey Beach showed smart form when third three starts back and a winner four starts back, and he arrives on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going from stall one on 135 lb; the concern is his two more recent below-par efforts.

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Linda Perratt — the trainer also saddles Monhammer today — who has winning form at 7f on good ground and ran third here on this course last season; 18 days between runs is not a concern and Oisin McSweeney should slot her just off Filey Beach's quarters to maximise the pace scenario that suits her.
runners_data.comment: Keep Me Stable arrives with distance and going experience in her favour, and a win five starts back gives her a proven route to the frame; the risk is that her last two outings — unplaced and then eighth — suggest she needs to rediscover that form sharpish.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Courage
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has placed four times in her last five comparable starts but is still seeking a win; Luke Morris takes the ride for John Ryan whose yard is winless in the last 14 days, and her lack of course form at Musselburgh is a mild flag, though good ground and 7f suit her profile cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Chloe's Courage faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and was third two starts back, suggesting she isn't entirely without ability.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with a string of placed efforts on good ground at this trip — her last four runs read 2-4-3-2 — but she is a true hold-up horse whose natural rearward position is unavailable in this small, pace-light field; running from a compressed midfield rather than off a true strong pace means her finishing kick is likely to be blunted, and the STYLE_FIT tag is warranted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Misemerald nevertheless arrives in decent nick just seven days after finishing second, and has run over today's distance and going before — but with an official mark of 46 and ranked fifth of six on our figures, she faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Maui Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Wilf Storey returning after 34 days off — the longest absence in the field — with a form string that shows no wins or places on good turf at 7f; Greg Fairley rides but the profile here is uninspiring, and stepping up slightly in trip from recent 6f runs adds an untested dimension.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Maui Breeze does at least bring experience of today's trip and going, and a 34-day break may have freshened her; fifth two starts back is her best recent showing, and she merits consideration from stall two on a respectable speed figure.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 7f on good ground and has a solid record in this grade, but his natural style is to come from well off the pace — a setup that simply will not materialise in a six-runner field with a single controlled front-runner; Paul Mulrennan will likely find him closer to the action than ideal, and his REDISTRIBUTED tag honestly reflects that his finishing run may lack the full power it would carry from further back.
runners_data.comment: Monhammer bounced back to winning ways last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, giving him a live chance from stall four carrying 128 lb; the worry is whether he can back it up on just a week's turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Filey Beach is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no credible challenger for the lead, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off over Musselburgh's flat seven furlongs. Keep Me Stable is the most likely to press from a prominent position and could sit just off Filey Beach's shoulder, but with only six runners and no genuine pace duel brewing, the tempo should remain measured rather than truly searching. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Monhammer and Misemerald are genuine come-from-behind horses who will be compressed into midfield rather than finding their true rearward berth, meaning they lose their natural rhythm advantage and the tactical edge that suits them. A controlled, uncontested pace from Filey Beach on good going over a flat track strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than closers who need a fast tempo to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Filey Beach Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Filey Beach dictates a comfortable gallop from the front and no rival applies sustained pressure through the first half.
scenarios.body: Filey Beach sets a measured pace with Keep Me Stable tracking, and neither is pressed hard enough to empty reserves before the straight, leaving the prominent duo in command at the two-furlong pole; on good Musselburgh turf with a flat run-in, a horse that has led throughout faces minimal late challenge from hold-up types who never got into a true rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Picks Up Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough through the first four furlongs to soften Filey Beach before the straight, allowing a midfield horse to close.
scenarios.body: Monhammer, who has a strong record at 7f on good ground and a win last time out, is the most likely beneficiary if the front end fades in the final furlong; however, both Monhammer and Misemerald are operating out of their natural hold-up role here, which reduces the probability that either delivers a truly effective late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Suits Chloe
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a steady, attritional grind where hold-up horses fail to fire and a consistent forwardly-placed type grinds through.
scenarios.body: Chloe's Courage, a genuine hold-up mare with placed form at this trip and going, could pick her way through a compressed midfield if the race pace is honest enough to string the field out; she is the cleanest hold-up operator in the race without any redistribution flag and offers each-way value if the shape unexpectedly suits late runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Filey Beach or Keep Me Stable is checked or loses momentum early, causing a scrambled finish with no true front-end control.
scenarios.body: In a chaotic scenario where the expected leader vacates the role, Keep Me Stable or Monhammer could pick up the pieces from wherever they find themselves in the order; this scenario is low-probability given the small field, flat course, and Filey Beach's established front-running profile.

watchPoints.text: Filey Beach's weight burden of 135lbs is the single biggest danger flag — if she feels that in the final furlong after setting a controlled pace, Keep Me Stable is ideally positioned to pounce.

Linda Perratt saddles both Keep Me Stable and Monhammer — watch for any stable-orders dynamic where Monhammer's jockey Paul Mulrennan is asked to make more use of him than usual, which could inject unexpected pace into the race and alter the shape.

Misemerald and Monhammer are both operating out of their true hold-up roles in this small field — if neither can reproduce their best finishing kick from a compressed midfield, the race result is likely to be determined entirely by the front two.

Maui Breeze's 34-day absence and absence of any good-ground 7f placed form make her an unlikely disruptor, but monitor her market movement — any significant support could suggest a yard confidence angle that the form book does not show.
